newsitem.title: USA: Chesapeake, Va., approves $400 mln center.
newsitem.headline: Chesapeake, Va., approves $400 mln center.

text.p: Chesapeake, Va., City Council approved plans to build a $400 million conference center and agreed to raise hotel and meal taxes to fund the project, Virginian-Pilot reported Wednesday.
Both proposals passed in 7-2 votes Tuesday. The action raises the lodging tax to six percent from five percent, and raises the meal tax to 5.5 percent from five percent.
The 51,000-square-foot conference center will be built by a public-private partnership among the city, its Industrial Development Authority and a local builder, Armada/Hoffler.
Plans call for Armada/Hoffler to build the facility for $9 million on land it owns. The city will lease the building for $880,971 annually for 30 years, through the development authority.

The city will have an option to buy the center within the first year for $8.9 million. The purchase option will be renewed annually, with the price rising to $100 million if exercised in the 30th year of the contract.

Restaurant owners opposed the tax increase, saying they would derive no benefit from the conference center. Other objections were raised by residents who said the city is facing tough financial times and should concentrate on more essential projects, such as schools and roads.
Supporters of the project said the meeting center would help lure new businesses to Chesapeake.
